title: Policy compliance harness for regional tier routing and fallback model admissibility
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, reproducible compliance harness that validates routing policy DSLs against regional selection rules, tier affinity constraints, and fallback model admissibility. The harness should provide: 1) static schema checks and semantic linting for policy files, 2) a stochastic simulator that replays sampled traffic to surface mismatches between declared routing intent and actual resolution, 3) an explainable scoring mechanism for policy conformance (e.g., region affinity score, tier safety score, fallback admissibility score), and 4) CI gates and a runtime feature flag to opt into strict vs permissive enforcement during staged rollout. Goal: reduce incidents and misroutes during large rollouts and provide actionable diagnostics for PM/Design/Support teams.
acceptance_criteria: A schema validator that rejects invalid field types and unknown rule keys with readable error messages
A semantic linter that warns about likely misconfigurations (e.g., region+tier incompatible pairs, missing fallback variant for critical models)
A simulation harness that can replay 24h of sampled traffic and produce a per-policy conformance report within 30m for 100k sampled requests
A conformance scoring output (JSON lines) with per-rule breakdown and suggested remediation hints
Unit tests covering schema and linter rules, integration tests for the simulator against fixture traffic
CI integration that fails pull requests if policy changes reduce conformance score by >10% for guarded releases
tasks: Design schema extension for fallback.admissibility and tier.affinity fields
Implement JSON Schema + supplemental semantic checks (TypeScript validator)
Prototype simulator that maps request metadata -> resolution graph and computes conformance metrics
Integrate linter output into Console policy upload flow and CLI (redwoodctl policy check)
Add CI pipeline job and perf budget for simulation run
Author runbook for on-call steps when policy conformance degrades
comments: 2026-02-24 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after post-mortem for incident INF-2026-02 where a regional tier mismatch routed traffic to an incompatible GPU pool. Proposed a simulator to catch these before deploy.

2026-03-01 Noah Ruiz: Spiked a prototype TypeScript validator. JSON Schema covers most shape issues but semantic checks (e.g., model.variant.compatible_with.region) need custom rules. Performance looks OK for single-file linting but simulator needs careful sampling to be performant.
2026-03-03 Ava Patel (PM): Prioritize clear remediation messages. Support needs exact delta lines to communicate to customers. Also request an early Console integration for policy preview in PR flow.

2026-03-05 Sofia Martinez (Security): Reviewed schema for sensitive fields. Recommend flagging policies that reference private model variants without proper access scope. Security review flagged in ticket.
2026-03-07 Liam O'Connor: Implemented basic conformance score prototype and added score breakdown per rule. Pushed draft PR for validator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14222

2026-03-08 Maya Chen: Running simulation on last 48h sample to validate runtime budget. Observed that naive replay tries to evaluate expensive fallback paths; added heuristics to cap deep fallback exploration to keep runtime within target.
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Chose JSON Schema + supplemental TypeScript semantic checks rather than moving to a new DSL format to minimize disruption to existing policy authors.
2026-03-04: Opted for a decoupled simulator that runs offline in CI and produces artifacts instead of a blocking runtime check to avoid adding latency to control plane uploads.

2026-03-06: Agreed on gradual enforcement: warn-only in initial cycles, then optional strict mode behind a runtime feature flag for critical customers. Enforcement kickoff to be gated by a >90% conformance baseline.
notes: Trade-offs: strict validation reduces live incidents but increases churn for customers who rely on permissive defaults (e.g., region fallback to nearest available). We will include an auto-fix suggestion layer where possible.
Performance: simulation runtime scales with sample size and policy complexity. Introduced heuristics to prioritize critical rules and collapse identical resolution paths for large-scale traffic.
Observability: produce artifacts consumable by Console (policy preview, per-request simulated resolution trace) to aid debug.
Next steps: finish TypeScript validator, wire CLI policy check, add simulator orchestration in CI, and schedule security review follow-up with Sofia.
